items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: I got an offer to go with Ben Pollack... I remember that I was playing with the Pollack band, in New York

ctx.x: So he has to be given credit for that, don't you think.

Yes, of course. Of course, I knew him a long time and I think the credit I would give him doesn't go in that direction. It's this; it has to do with the marvelous enthusiasm he had and how helpful he was to me when I made my first recording with the Condou-Carmen McKenzie Chicagoans, Nobody's Sweetheart, and incidentally, it was on the strength of that that I got an offer to go with Ben Pollack and got out of Chicago and went to New York,

which was the place to be in those days. Because of Chicago supported jazz for a few years, and then of course, when Louis and all the greats left, went east to New York, we followed, because we felt that New York was the place that then could afford to support jazz and one could actually make a living playing music, jazz. There were so many recordings.
